title: Why 6 and 8 pay 5 times more than 2 and 12
description:
Two dice make 36 combinations, and they don't share them evenly. A 2 or a 12 needs one exact pair (1-1 or 6-6), but a 6 or an 8 can be made 5 ways each (2-6, 3-5, 4-4, 5-3, 6-2), so over 36 rolls a spot on 6 and 8 pays about 10 times while a spot on 2 and 12 pays twice. The 7 is the most common roll of all (6 ways, 1 in 6), which is why board games like Catan give it no tile. The dots under each number token are exactly its ways out of 36: add them up, and a 6-8-5 corner expects 14 cards every 36 rolls against 4 for a 2-12-3 corner.

Numbers checked in code: all 36 combinations counted, plus 1,000,000 simulated rolls (6 and 8 came up 4.99 times as often as 2 and 12). Sources: Wikipedia, Catan; Stanford CS, Dice Odds for Settlers of Catan.

social_caption: A board-game corner on 6 and 8 pays five times as often as one on 2 and 12. Here's how to count it from two dice.
facts_checked: Two dice: 36 ordered combinations; 2 and 12 one way each; 6 and 8 five ways each (2-6, 3-5, 4-4, 5-3, 6-2); 7 six ways = 1 in 6 (verify.py, full enumeration)
Catan: two six-sided dice decide which hexes produce; a settlement next to the rolled number gets one card; a 7 moves the robber (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catan)
Number tokens carry dots equal to the ways out of 36 (one dot on 2/12 up to five on 6/8), and there is no 7 token (https://cs.stanford.edu/people/nick/settlers/DiceOddsSettlers.html)

beats.say: 6 and 8, or 2 and 12? One pays five times more.
Each number gets one roll at a time, so it feels even. It isn't.
Two dice make 36 combinations. Count how many land on each total.
A 12 needs six and six. One way. A 2 needs one and one. One way.
An 8 has five ways. Two and six, three and five, four and four, five and three, six and two. Same for 6.
So every 36 rolls, your 6 and 8 pay 10 times. Your 2 and 12 pay twice.
But the most common roll isn't on the board at all.
7 has six ways. One roll in six. And it pays nobody. That's the robber.
Those dots under each number? They're its ways. So just add the dots.
A corner on 6, 8 and 5 gets 14 cards every 36 rolls. 2, 12 and 3 gets 4.
So your corner touches 4, 9 and 10. How many dots is that?
